# Exact staircase triangulation of an ambient-simplex slice

This is a finite, exact version of the projective-product cap calculus.
It retains arbitrary ambient normals. A bounded check on the
height multiset (0,0,0,1,3,3,4) rejects a floating-point apparent
counterexample at the own middle centroid. No all-cap safety claim
or depth minimum is inferred from those finitely many checks.

Let C be a full (d+1)-simplex with vertices (h_i,xi_i). At a level z
strictly between its minimum and maximum heights put

    I={i:h_i<z}, J={j:h_j>z}, E={e:h_e=z}.

Write a=|I|, b=|J|, c=|E|, so a+b+c=d+2.
For i in I and j in J define the actual edge-intersection vertex

    v_ij(z)=[(h_j-z)xi_i+(z-h_i)xi_j]/(h_j-h_i).

The section is the join of the equal-height vertex simplex
conv{xi_e:e in E} and the section with all equal-height barycentrics
zero. The join decomposition follows directly by separating the
total barycentric weight on E. The second factor is projectively
equivalent to Delta_(a-1) x Delta_(b-1), by the positive-denominator
map proved in ambient-simplex-barycentric-lattice-count-and-exact-slice-cap-calculus.md.
Its product vertices map precisely to v_ij(z).

Order I and J arbitrarily. Triangulate the product by monotone
staircase paths from (0,0) to (a-1,b-1), increasing one coordinate
at each step. For each path take its a+b-1 vertices v_ij and append
all c equal-height vertices. Their convex hull is a d-simplex.
These choose(a+b-2,a-1) simplices cover the actual section with
disjoint interiors. Indeed the standard staircase cells partition
the product, a projective map with positive denominator preserves
convex hulls and intersections, and joining with the equal-height
simplex preserves this partition. Thus this construction also
handles queried knot levels without any horizontal-interface limit.

For rational input all vertex coordinates and volumes are rational:

    |Q|=|det(q_1-q_0,...,q_d-q_0)|/d!.

For an arbitrary affine cap function L on the actual ambient space,
evaluate its margins t_k=L(z,q_k) at each simplex vertex. The
simplex's cap fraction is

    [t_0,...,t_d] (t)_+^d.

Use Hermite divided differences for repeated projected margins.
When all margins are nonnegative the closed cap is full; when all
are nonpositive and at least one is negative its volume is zero.
A cap whose restriction to the whole simplex is identically zero
is full under the closed convention. These explicit constant
cases retain possible vertical or identically zero restrictions.
Summing these exact simplex cap volumes gives the original slice
cap volume for every normal at a strict interior level.

At either extreme height, the closed section is exactly the convex
hull of the vertices having that height. If there are d+1 such
vertices, it is a full d-dimensional simplex: use its actual
d-volume and the direct simplex margin formula above, including
full closed caps whose restriction is identically zero. If fewer
than d+1 vertices have that extreme height, the section has zero
d-volume and contributes zero. Levels outside the height interval
are empty. These endpoint cases are essential because an integer
extreme height can carry a whole positive-volume facet.

After adding these closed endpoint contributions, summing over
integer z gives the full mixed cap mass. This is a calculation formula, not a
reduction to a finite list of cap directions.

For the exact simplex in
candidate 64c5bdbc0c6d6575, the
positive slices z=1,2,3 have respectively 6,10,1 staircase
simplices. Their exact volume sums agree with
V(139/288,1/2,1/32).

At its own middle centroid g_2, consider the rational oblique cap

    (z-2)+(x_3-g_2,3)+12(x_4-g_2,4)+(x_5-g_2,5)>=0.

The exact normalized mass is

    22871381014142276443/99086463923756728320,

about 0.23082246, above Gamma_5/2. A second rational normal close
to a floating numerical optimizer, in coordinates (z,x_1,...,x_5),
is

    (51/500,0,3/40000,103/1000,251/200,121/1000).

Its through-g_2 cap has exact normalized mass

    40785603200965569268246734952488254693
    /176707994235590558388120820688145530880,

about 0.23080791, also above the target. A naive floating divided
difference evaluated a nearby direction below the target because
nearly repeated projected knots caused cancellation. That output
was never accepted as a certificate. These rational checks leave
the own-middle-centroid all-cap question open.

The standard-library verifier
../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_ambient_simplex_staircase_cap_checks.py checks all three
exact slice volume sums and five exact oblique cap evaluations.
